============================================================
1. PACKAGES FOR DATASETS AND FILES
============================================================

dataset_packages <- c( "readr", "readxl", "writexl", "haven", "dplyr" )

missing_packages <- dataset_packages[ !dataset_packages %in% rownames(installed.packages()) ]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) { install.packages(missing_packages) }

invisible( lapply(dataset_packages, library, character.only = TRUE) )

============================================================
1.1 CREATING A SAMPLE DATASET
============================================================

student_id <- 1:8

student_name <- c( "Brian", "Sandra", "Joseph", "Alice", "Patrick", "Diane", "Michael", "Grace" )

age <- c(22, 24, 27, 21, 25, 23, 28, 26)

gender <- c( "Male", "Female", "Male", "Female", "Male", "Female", "Male", "Female" )

department <- c( "Finance", "IT", "Economics", "Management", "IT", "Finance", "Management", "Economics" )

marks <- c(75, 88, 67, 92, 81, 79, 85, 90)

student_data <- data.frame( student_id, student_name, age, gender, department, marks )

student_data

============================================================
1.2 IMPORTING CSV DATA
============================================================

dir.create("assignment1_data", showWarnings = FALSE)

write.csv( student_data, "assignment1_data/students.csv", row.names = FALSE )

csv_data <- read.csv( "assignment1_data/students.csv" )

csv_data

readr_data <- readr::read_csv( "assignment1_data/students.csv", show_col_types = FALSE )

head(readr_data)

str(readr_data)

summary(readr_data)

============================================================
1.3 IMPORTING EXCEL DATA
============================================================

writexl::write_xlsx( student_data, "assignment1_data/students.xlsx" )

excel_data <- readxl::read_excel( "assignment1_data/students.xlsx" )

excel_data

head(excel_data)

names(excel_data)

str(excel_data)

summary(excel_data)

============================================================
1.4 IMPORTING TEXT FILES
============================================================

write.table( student_data, "assignment1_data/students.txt", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE )

text_data <- read.table( "assignment1_data/students.txt", header = TRUE )

text_data

head(text_data)

str(text_data)

============================================================
1.5 IMPORTING SPSS DATA
============================================================

haven::write_sav( student_data, "assignment1_data/students.sav" )

spss_data <- haven::read_sav( "assignment1_data/students.sav" )

spss_data

head(spss_data)

str(spss_data)

summary(spss_data)

============================================================
1.6 IMPORTING STATA DATA
============================================================

haven::write_dta( student_data, "assignment1_data/students.dta" )

stata_data <- haven::read_dta( "assignment1_data/students.dta" )

stata_data

head(stata_data)

str(stata_data)

1.7 IMPORTING SAS DATA
============================================================

if (file.exists("assignment1_data/students.sas7bdat")) {

sas_data <- haven::read_sas( "assignment1_data/students.sas7bdat" )

}

============================================================
1.9 DATA MANAGEMENT USING DPLYR
============================================================

selected_students <- dplyr::select( student_data, student_name, department, marks )

selected_students

high_performers <- dplyr::filter( student_data, marks >= 80 )

high_performers

updated_students <- dplyr::mutate( student_data, performance = ifelse( marks >= 85, "Excellent", "Good" ) )

updated_students

sorted_students <- dplyr::arrange( student_data, desc(marks) )

sorted_students

department_summary <- student_data %>% group_by(department) %>% summarise( average_marks = mean(marks), highest_marks = max(marks), total_students = n(), .groups = "drop" )

department_summary

============================================================
2. PACKAGES FOR POSTGRESQL DATABASES
============================================================

postgres_packages <- c( "DBI", "RPostgres" )

missing_packages <- postgres_packages[ !postgres_packages %in% rownames(installed.packages()) ]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) { install.packages(missing_packages) }

invisible( lapply(postgres_packages, library, character.only = TRUE) )

============================================================
2.1 CONNECTING TO A POSTGRESQL DATABASE
============================================================
Set your database credentials before running this section.

database_name <- Sys.getenv("PGDATABASE") database_host <- Sys.getenv("PGHOST") database_user <- Sys.getenv("PGUSER") database_password <- Sys.getenv("PGPASSWORD")

if ( nzchar(database_name) && nzchar(database_host) && nzchar(database_user) && nzchar(database_password) ) {

connection <- tryCatch( DBI::dbConnect( RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = database_name, host = database_host, port = 5432, user = database_user, password = database_password ), error = function(e) { message("Database connection failed: ", conditionMessage(e)) NULL } )

if (!is.null(connection)) {

DBI::dbListTables(connection)

if ("students" %in% DBI::dbListTables(connection)) {

  postgres_data <- DBI::dbReadTable(
    connection,
    "students"
  )

  print(head(postgres_data))

  print(summary(postgres_data))

}

DBI::dbDisconnect(connection)


}

} else {

message( "PostgreSQL credentials are not configured. Set PGDATABASE, PGHOST, PGUSER and PGPASSWORD to connect." )

}

============================================================
3. PACKAGES FOR APPLICATION PROGRAMMING INTERFACES (APIs)
============================================================

api_packages <- c( "httr2", "jsonlite" )

missing_packages <- api_packages[ !api_packages %in% rownames(installed.packages()) ]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) { install.packages(missing_packages) }

invisible( lapply(api_packages, library, character.only = TRUE) )

============================================================
3.1 CONNECTING TO A PUBLIC API
============================================================

api_result <- tryCatch({

response <- httr2::request( "https://api.github.com" ) |> httr2::req_timeout(15) |> httr2::req_perform()

api_text <- httr2::resp_body_string(response)

api_data <- jsonlite::fromJSON(api_text)

print(api_data)

api_data

}, error = function(e) {

message( "API request could not be completed: ", conditionMessage(e) )

NULL

})

============================================================
3.2 EXPLORING API INFORMATION
============================================================

if (!is.null(api_result)) {

names(api_result)

str(api_result)

}

============================================================
4. PACKAGES FOR RANDOM OR SIMULATED DATA
============================================================

random_packages <- c( "randomNames", "wakefield" )

missing_packages <- random_packages[ !random_packages %in% rownames(installed.packages()) ]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) { install.packages(missing_packages) }

invisible( lapply(random_packages, library, character.only = TRUE) )

============================================================
4.1 GENERATING RANDOM STUDENT DATA
============================================================

set.seed(2026)

random_students <- data.frame( student_id = 1:10, age = sample(18:30, 10, replace = TRUE), marks = sample(40:100, 10, replace = TRUE), attendance = sample(60:100, 10, replace = TRUE), gender = sample( c("Male", "Female"), 10, replace = TRUE ) )

random_students

============================================================
4.2 GENERATING RANDOM NAMES
============================================================

random_student_names <- c( "Daniel", "Esther", "Samuel", "Olivia", "Andrew", "Beatrice", "Peter", "Martha", "Felix", "Diana" )

random_students$student_name <- random_student_names

random_students

============================================================
4.3 ANALYZING SIMULATED DATA
============================================================

summary(random_students)

mean(random_students$marks)

max(random_students$marks)

min(random_students$marks)

============================================================
4.4 CREATING PERFORMANCE CATEGORIES
============================================================

random_students$performance <- ifelse( random_students$marks >= 80, "Excellent", ifelse( random_students$marks >= 60, "Good", "Needs Improvement" ) )

random_students

table(random_students$performance)

============================================================
6. DATA VISUALIZATION
============================================================
6.1 Bar Chart

barplot( table(random_students$performance), main = "Student Performance Categories", xlab = "Performance", ylab = "Number of Students", col = "lightblue" )

6.2 Histogram

hist( random_students$marks, main = "Distribution of Student Marks", xlab = "Examination Marks", col = "lightgreen", border = "black" )

6.3 Scatter Plot

plot( random_students$age, random_students$marks, main = "Student Age and Examination Marks", xlab = "Age", ylab = "Marks", pch = 19, col = "blue" )

6.4 Boxplot

boxplot( marks ~ gender, data = random_students, main = "Marks Comparison by Gender", xlab = "Gender", ylab = "Marks", col = c("lightpink", "lightblue") )
